title: Consumer project configuration v1
description: Craft project configuration in `.craft/project.json`. Every field except `formatVersion` is optional; an absent field takes the default shown.

provider.description: Provider name: `git`, `github`, `gitlab`, or your own such as `jira`. `github` and `gitlab` CLI bindings get built-in change operations.

host.description: Code host name, such as `gitlab.example.com`. Nothing infers it from remotes.

repository.description: Repository path on the host, such as `team/project`.

operations.description: Exact mappings by operation name. They take precedence over built-in mappings.

args.description: CLI arguments. `{name}` placeholders are filled from the operation parameters; the plan runs without a shell.

provider.description: Provider name: `git`, `github`, `gitlab`, or your own such as `jira`. `github` and `gitlab` CLI bindings get built-in change operations.

command.description: Not used by MCP bindings; accepted for symmetry.

host.description: Code host name, such as `gitlab.example.com`. Nothing infers it from remotes.

repository.description: Repository path on the host, such as `team/project`.

operations.description: Exact mappings by operation name. They take precedence over built-in mappings.

tool.description: Exact MCP tool name the host exposes.

arguments.description: Tool arguments; string values may hold `{name}` placeholders; a whole-value placeholder keeps the parameter's JSON type.

service.description: One service binding: a CLI (`transport: "cli"`) or an MCP server (`transport: "mcp"`).

$schema.description: Optional link to this schema for editor completion and hover help. Craft ignores the value.

languages.description: Languages the code is written in. Selects language guidance; nothing else is inferred from it. Default for modules that declare none.

layers.description: Application layers: `ui`, `backend` or `agent`. Selects layer guidance. Default for modules that declare none.

frameworks.description: Frameworks in use, such as `react`. Selects framework guidance when Craft has it. Default for modules that declare none.

providers.description: Model or cloud providers in use, such as `foundry`. Selects provider guidance when Craft has it. Default for modules that declare none.

modules.description: Parts of the repository with an owner, stack and checks. Routes name the modules a change touches, their dependents and their checks. Without modules the project is one unit.

name.description: Unique lowercase name (letters, digits, hyphens) used in `dependsOn`, scopes and routes.

path.description: Project-relative folder the module owns. The most specific path owns a file.

owner.description: Team or person shown as the owner in routes.

languages.description: Languages the code is written in. Selects language guidance; nothing else is inferred from it. Overrides the project value; an empty array clears it.

layers.description: Application layers: `ui`, `backend` or `agent`. Selects layer guidance. Overrides the project value; an empty array clears it.

skills.description: Logical skills (`package:skill`) added to routes for `implement`, `plan`, `investigate` and `review` work in this module.

dependsOn.description: Modules this module may import. With `hexagonal-architecture`, `clean-architecture` or a `module-dependencies` check, an added import into any other declared module is reported. Absent: imports are not checked.

providers.description: Model or cloud providers in use, such as `foundry`. Selects provider guidance when Craft has it. Overrides the project value; an empty array clears it.

frameworks.description: Frameworks in use, such as `react`. Selects framework guidance when Craft has it. Overrides the project value; an empty array clears it.

checks.description: Commands that verify this module, run in the module's path. Routes list them as argv; `craft check` runs those of the changed modules without a shell and reports each result. Craft never runs them from a hook or assumes they pass.

id.description: Name of the check in `craft check` results. Default: the module name and the check's position, such as `api-1`.

stage.description: When `craft check` runs the command: at each step, before a commit, before a pull request or in CI. A run at one stage includes the earlier stages and lists later ones as left to their stage, never as passed.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds `craft check` lets the command run before ending it and reporting it as timed out.

runtimes.description: Runtimes in use, such as `node`. TypeScript does not imply Node; declare it. Overrides the project value; an empty array clears it.

standards.description: Project standards: consumer-owned declarations routed by scope and, for anchors, checked without a model.

items.description: One standard: an `id` and one source (`file`, `folder`, `anchor`, `checklist` or `run`).

id.description: Stable handle shown in routes and check results.

anchor.description: An established standard by name: a Semantic Anchors catalog id, a Craft alias such as semver, or an id from the project's anchor catalogs. Names with a Craft check are checked deterministically; others are advised or reviewed.

summary.description: One line shown in routes instead of the standard's content.

level.description: advise: named when work reaches the scope; check: an anchor check or a run command; review: a checklist. Defaults from the declaration's form.

scope.description: Where the standard applies; all keys must match, any value within a key. Absent: the whole project.

paths.description: Project-relative path prefixes of the affected files.

intents.description: Kinds of work: story, plan, verify, explore, review, implement and the other routing intents.

run.description: A consumer command that checks the standard. The agent is told to run it, and `craft check` runs it without a shell for changed files in the standard's scope.

command.description: Executable the agent runs to check the standard.

cwd.description: Project-relative working directory. Default: the project root.

stage.description: When `craft check` runs the command: at each step, before a commit, before a pull request or in CI. A run at one stage includes the earlier stages and lists later ones as left to their stage, never as passed.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds `craft check` lets the command run before ending it and reporting it as timed out.

checklist.description: Items shown with the route and in the stop review when work reaches the scope. Defaults `level` to `review`.

anchors.description: Where the project's own anchors come from and which Craft defaults apply. A project entry replaces the built-in entry with the same id.

catalogs.description: Project-relative anchor catalog files, read in order; a later file wins on the same id. Each holds {"anchors": [{id, title?, summary?, checklist?, check?, intents?, targets?}]}.

items.description: Project-relative path of one catalog file.

defaults.description: Whether Craft adds its anchors for the kind of work to routes, advised and never checked; off unless true. A declared standard for the kind of work replaces them.

disables.description: Anchors Craft must not add as defaults.

items.description: Anchor id or alias; it must resolve.

skills.description: The project's own skills in routes. Hosts list project skills themselves; a declaration tells Craft which one a route recommends. Routes name them project:<name>; hosts are shown the bare name.

declared.description: Project skills to name in routes.

items.description: One project skill. Needs `replaces`, `scope` or both.

name.description: The name in the skill's SKILL.md front matter.

path.description: The skill folder at the project root. A host that does not read this folder keeps the package skill and the route reports why.

replaces.description: Package skills this skill takes the place of wherever a route selects them; one declaration per package skill.

scope.description: Where the skill applies, as for standards: with replaces it narrows the replacement, alone it adds the skill to matching routes.

paths.description: Project-relative path prefixes of the affected files.

intents.description: Kinds of work: story, plan, verify, explore, review, implement and the other routing intents.

disables.description: Package skills routes no longer recommend. Hosts may still list them; Craft never edits host configuration.

services.description: Git, code host and tracker bindings that `craft operation` turns into CLI or MCP invocation plans. Nothing here runs a command or opens a connection; authentication stays with the host.

git.description: Local Git. Default: the `git` CLI. See Service bindings.

codehost.description: Pull or merge requests: `gh` for GitHub, `glab` for GitLab, or exact operation mappings. See Service bindings.

tasks.description: Task tracker. Always needs explicit operation mappings. See Service bindings.

permissions.description: Which mutating service operations may be planned at all. Each still needs separate authorization when it runs.

writeOperations.description: Write operations `craft operation` may plan. Default: none, so every mutation is refused.

execution.description: Worker roles, model profiles and host support. Logical names only; nothing vendor-specific is built in, and nothing here starts a worker or switches a model.

roles.description: How each kind of work runs. Defaults: `locator` uses a tool with the `economical` profile, `reviewer` runs in the main session with `strong`, the others in the main session with `standard`.

mode.description: `main`: in the current session. `delegate`: a worker, when the host allows it. `tool`: a deterministic tool first.
`main`: in the current session. `delegate`: a worker, when the host allows it. `tool`: a deterministic tool first.
`main`: in the current session. `delegate`: a worker, when the host allows it. `tool`: a deterministic tool first.

`main`: in the current session. `delegate`: a worker, when the host allows it. `tool`: a deterministic tool first.

hosts.description: What each host supports, keyed by host name (`claude`, `codex`, ...).

delegation.description: The host can start workers. Delegated roles are planned only when both the role and the host allow it.

models.description: Exact host model name for each profile name.

additionalProperties.description: Exact model name the host accepts.

mainModelSwitch.description: Explicit host support declaration; never grants permission to switch models.

contextLimits.description: Context limits by exact host model name, over the bundled host table. windowTokens applies only when the host reports no window; budgetTokens is an optional working budget past which advice suggests resuming from the checkpoint in a new session.

profiles.description: Named model profiles that roles refer to. Defaults: `economical` escalates to `standard`, `standard` to `strong`.

capabilities.description: Capability tags the profile offers, used when advice asks for one.

maxAttempts.description: Failed attempts on the same task and revision before advice escalates. Default: 3.

escalateTo.description: Profile to recommend after `maxAttempts`. Absent: advice stops instead of inventing a stronger model.

class.description: Logical class: `economical` (lookups, formatting, deterministic checks), `standard` (routine work) or `strong` (hard review and design).

enabled.description: Save a snapshot at turn end and context transitions, and show the session identity and resume lines.

readOnly.description: Deny common `gh`/`glab` publishing commands and `git push` from the shell in this project. A heuristic, not a replacement for read-only credentials.

safety.description: Opt-in rules that refuse destructive shell commands and commands that reach outside the project, on hosts where a hook can refuse a tool call. A rule only refuses: nothing here approves a command, and the host's own prompts, sandbox and deny rules keep applying. A guardrail, not a security boundary; `craft settings` lists the rules in force.

enabled.description: Turn the policy on. Off, no command is refused.

deny.description: The project's own rules: a command whose leading words match is refused.

items.description: One rule: an `id`, the leading words of the command and why it is refused.

id.description: Stable handle named in the refusal.

command.description: Leading words of the command, such as `terraform`, `destroy`. The executable matches by name with or without a path; variable assignments and wrappers such as `env` before it are skipped.

reason.description: What the rule refuses, shown with the refusal.

runtimes.description: Runtimes in use, such as `node`. TypeScript does not imply Node; declare it. Default for modules that declare none.

routing.description: Switches for what hooks show the agent or record. Each also takes personal preferences and task overrides; `craft settings` shows where each value came from.

promptHints.description: Routing hints on prompts. Set false to keep the request's intent as session state without showing a hint.

editHints.description: Routing hints when the agent edits a file: the skills and references for the edited scope.

dedupeHints.description: Session-scoped routing hint hash state; no prompts or evidence are stored. Set false to disable.

standardChecks.description: Deterministic anchor checks after an edit or commit in a declared standard's scope. Set false to keep standards in routes without checking.

stopReview.description: When a turn ends after changing files, one summary of new findings (module dependencies, debt markers) and the declared review items of the changed scope; the host continues the turn once to address it. Set false to never hold a stop.

debtMarkers.description: Report debt markers a change adds against HEAD in the stop summary: TODO/FIXME comments, lint or type-check suppressions, skipped tests, removed assertions.

testRuns.description: Record each test command the host runs with its verdict and the tree it ran on, tell the model at once when a run executed no test, and restate the runs on resume. Set false to record and show none; a declared verification pass is then not checked against an observed run.

workerStandards.description: Give a subagent the host starts the checked and reviewed standards of the delegating session's scope. Set false to start workers without them.

sessionRecords.description: Keep the session's established intent, its routed files and planning evidence, and the pending-resume mark under .craft/state. Set false to write none; features that read them then see no established work.

sessionSummary.description: When a turn ends, show the user one line on what Craft did in the session (standards findings raised and fixed, test runs that ran no test, lookups answered, task contexts restored), where the host displays a hook's message and only when the line changed. Set false to show none; `craft session` still reports the counts. Needs sessionRecords.

conventionProposals.description: When a session starts in a project that declares no standards, say once how many its own files support (conventions named in agent instructions or the contributor document, lint and format configuration) and that `craft standards --propose` lists them. Said again only when the set changes. Set false to never scan at session start.

projectChecks.description: Let `craft check` run the commands declared in `modules[].checks` and `standards[].run`. Set false to have it run nothing and say so; routes still list the commands for the agent to run.

efficiency.description: Session advice: lookups, attempts, review, context and delegation. Recommendations only; Craft never acts on them itself.

enabled.description: Answer certain lookups (callers, declarations, configuration keys, mentions, decision records) in the hook, without a model turn.

reuse.description: Reuse earlier `craft locate` results in a task while revision, files and configuration are unchanged.

batching.description: Accepted for policy files. Batching independent tool calls is a workflow instruction; `craft` does not act on these values.

enabled.description: Recorded only; the budget below always applies to recorded attempts.

maxAttempts.description: Same failure on unchanged source this many times: return control or escalate.

enabled.description: Give advice. False removes the next-step suggestion.

at.description: When advice is given. Only `meaningful-boundaries` exists.

mode.description: `manual`: no review offers. `recommend`: offer a review where it helps. `execute-when-authorized`: may proceed once the user approves the offer.

context.description: Context pressure advice. Bands must rise: `elevatedAt` < `compactAt` < `restartAt`, each a fraction of the window.

elevatedAt.description: Occupancy at which pressure is elevated.

compactAt.description: Occupancy at which advice is "checkpoint, then compact".

restartAt.description: Occupancy at which advice is "checkpoint, then new session".

action.description: `manual`: no compaction or restart advice. `recommend`: advise at a safe boundary. `execute-when-authorized`: may proceed once the user approves.

mode.description: `manual`: no worker plans. `recommend`: plan workers where a role and host allow it. `execute-when-authorized`: may proceed once the user approves.

maxWorkers.description: Most running workers per session. 0 disables worker plans.

workspace.description: Private scratch directories and promoted evidence under the state directory. `craft settings` shows the limits.

maxSessions.description: Most workspaces kept; at capacity the oldest inactive one is evicted first.

staleAfterHours.description: Hours without a write before `workspace-clean` treats a workspace as stale.

maxBytes.description: Most bytes in one scratch directory.

maxFiles.description: Most files in one scratch directory.

evidence.description: Files promoted from scratch as evidence.

enabled.description: Allow promoting scratch files as evidence.

maxBytes.description: Most bytes of promoted evidence per workspace.

evidence.description: Project Intelligence enablement and inventory scope.

enabled.description: Route structural lookups (declarations, callers, imports, document sections, links and mentions, decision records, configuration keys) through Project Intelligence before literal search. On unless set false.

exclude.description: Project-relative path prefixes left out of the evidence inventory, such as generated samples or vendored bundles. Whole path components; a trailing / is accepted.

items.description: Project-relative path prefix, matched by whole path components.
